clue.text: Crazy rocker retires, nursing inflammation

indicators.note: retires says the hidden letters are read backwards
the reversed words are nursing, holding within them, the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wild rock musician bows out of the scene, nursing some swelling or soreness.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'nursing inflammation' as the definition, but 'nursing' is the containment signal: 'Crazy rocker' read backwards, as 'retires' says, holds the answer. The definition is 'inflammation' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Coryza is the medical term for a head cold, the swelling of the nasal mucous membranes.

clue.text: Having equal pressure and current, or basic fuses

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: letters that fuse melt and run together into a new form, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sounds like an electrical engineering note about pressure, current and basic fuses in a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuses' looks like a noun in the wiring scene but is a verb signalling the anagram of OR BASIC, giving SOBARIC after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobaric is the meteorological and physics term for conditions or lines of constant, equal pressure.

clue.text: One's accompanying unbelievable organist

indicators.note: accompanying puts the one piece alongside the other, here one's following the tall piece

parts.note: a tall story or tall tale is an unbelievable one
one is I, and the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Someone playing along with an organist who is beyond belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tallis was the great Tudor composer who served as organist of the Chapel Royal.

clue.text: Chaps eating cold caviar he served professionally

indicators.note: the men piece eats, taking in, the letter for cold

parts.note: chaps are men
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
caviar is fish roe

explanation.surface: Men tucking into chilled caviar that a professional waiter has served them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' suggests a waiter, but it is tennis serving: John McEnroe was a professional player famous for his serve.
explanation.definitionFit: John McEnroe is the American tennis champion, a professional server on court.

clue.text: Very dull clothing earl changed

indicators.note: the dull piece is clothing, wrapping around, the letter for earl

parts.note: arid means dry and dull, uninteresting

explanation.surface: An earl's very drab outfit has been swapped for something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Something varied has been altered or made different, so the two words share a sense.

clue.text: Glass for alcohol preferably filled by taps

indicators.note: the preferably piece is filled by the taps letters placed inside it

parts.note: sooner means rather, preferably, as in I'd sooner not
taps are marked C and H, for cold and hot

explanation.surface: A drinker would rather have their glass topped up straight from the taps at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taps' suggests beer taps, but here it gives the letters C and H printed on bath or sink taps.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a tall glass for sherry or, in Australia, beer: a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Lake by Alps with Italian viewpoint

parts.note: con is the Italian word for with
a stance is a position or point of view on an issue

explanation.surface: A tourist enjoying a mountain lake from an Italian lookout point.
explanation.walkthrough: Every across answer is also a character of Shakespeare, the creator named at 17 across; Constance is Arthur's mother in King John.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Constance lies at the northern foot of the Alps, bordered by Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

clue.text: Knight's piercing spike

indicators.note: the knight's letter is piercing, so stuck inside, the spike piece

parts.note: to spike a drink is to lace it
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Describes a mounted knight's long pointed weapon used for skewering opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as is: the knight's letter is piercing the spike word. The whole clue also describes the answer, a knight's piercing weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is the long spear carried by a mounted knight, a pointed shaft made for piercing.

clue.text: Ancient chieftain's treated nicely, receiving honour

indicators.note: the reworked letters are receiving the honour inside them
treated as in processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: An old tribal chief, treated kindly, is given an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' signals rearranging NICELY into CYLINE, which takes in MBE; the 's of 'chieftain's' is read as is.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbeline, Shakespeare's title character, was an ancient British king, Cunobelinus, a tribal ruler.

clue.text: Character lacking tolerance from great books

parts.note: great means big
OT, the Old Testament, is the crossword's usual set of books

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded figure drawn from some weighty volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot is a person intolerant of opinions, races or creeds unlike their own.

clue.text: Third child registered in Somerset House

indicators.note: registered in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A family's third baby has its birth recorded at Somerset House.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset House in London long held the register of births, marriages and deaths for England and Wales, which makes 'registered in' a neat hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Seth is the third son of Adam and Eve, born after Cain and Abel.

clue.text: Back from market with a shaggy ox or bull

indicators.note: back from points to the final letter of market

parts.note: the urus is the aurochs, the wild ox of old Europe

explanation.surface: Buying a hairy ox or a bull at the cattle market.
explanation.walkthrough: The urus or aurochs is an extinct wild ox; 'or' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus is Latin for bull and the name of the zodiac sign and constellation shown as one.

clue.text: Extravagant party held by old French writer

indicators.note: the party word is held inside the writer's name

parts.note: Jules Verne was the French author of science fiction
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An over-the-top party hosted by an elderly French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdone means exaggerated or taken to excess, which is what extravagant behaviour is.

clue.text: Fast living lady has her heart stolen

parts.note: quick means alive, as in the quick and the dead

indicators.note: her heart stolen means the middle letters of lady are removed

explanation.surface: A woman living life in the fast lane falls in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has her heart stolen' reads as falling in love, but it removes AD, the middle of LADY, leaving LY. Mistress Quickly is the hostess in the Henry IV plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickly is the adverb for done fast, at speed, so the two are interchangeable.

clue.text: Completely in nude, one playing solo

indicators.note: the completely piece and one go in the rearranged nude letters
playing about with the word nude, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A naked performer giving a solo turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing solo' reads as a soloist's performance, but 'playing' is the anagram signal, making UNED, and 'solo' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unallied means without allies or partners, standing alone, which solo also conveys as an adjective.

clue.text: The French kings frolic

parts.note: la is the French feminine form of the
R, for rex, and K, from chess, both stand for king

explanation.surface: French monarchs having a playful romp.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a spree or bit of fun, a carefree escapade: the noun frolic exactly.

clue.text: Creator of across solutions shows amazing breadth

indicators.note: amazing as in astounding or putting in a maze, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Says that the setter of the across answers has shown remarkable range.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the theme clue: every across answer, from CONSTANCE to VALENTINE, is a Shakespeare character.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard of Avon is Shakespeare, who created all the characters entered across in this grid.

clue.text: Most of Brad Pitt's works offering possibilities for extra?

indicators.note: works as in working over, kneading the letters into new shape
most of Brad means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Asks whether Brad Pitt's films offer chances for an extra in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like his body of films but signals the anagram of BRA and PITTS. The question mark flags that an extra is a film walk-on, not something additional.
explanation.definitionFit: Bit parts are small acting roles, the kind of work an extra in a film might hope to graduate to.

clue.text: Amazing appeal by Republican to hold recount

indicators.note: by places Republican beside the rest, here at the end
the appeal letters are made to hold the recount word between them

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crossword shorthand for appeal
to recount a story is to tell it

explanation.surface: A Republican lodges a stunning appeal demanding the votes be counted again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recount' suggests an election recount, but it means narrate: TELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar is used informally for outstanding or brilliant, much as amazing is.

clue.text: Monsieur Arthur defends station of French princess

indicators.note: the Arthur piece defends the station by surrounding it

parts.note: Art is the short form of the name Arthur
gare is the French word for a railway station

explanation.surface: A gentleman named Arthur guards the railway station belonging to a French princess.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret of Anjou, the French princess who marries Henry VI, appears in four Shakespeare plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret of Anjou was a French royal daughter who became Henry VI's queen: a princess by birth.

clue.text: Not finishing Marx? He's a curmudgeon

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Groucho was the best known of the Marx Brothers comedy team

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone who never got through Karl Marx is a grumpy old type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marx' points to Karl and his unread volumes, but it is Groucho Marx, with his final O dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouch is a habitually grumpy, complaining person, the same sort as a curmudgeon.

clue.text: Stern and abstemious during prosperous time

indicators.note: the abstemious letters are placed during, inside, the prosperous time

parts.note: a boom is a period of economic prosperity
TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A severe, sober person who stays dry even in the boom years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like an adjective, but it is the back end of a ship; Bottom is also the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear of a ship, and colloquially a person's backside or rear end.

clue.text: Phone bill cuts I'll bring down

indicators.note: the word bill cuts out, losing, the letters of I'll

parts.note: the letters of I'll, without the apostrophe
to lower something is to bring it down

explanation.surface: A promise to reduce your phone bill by cutting costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill cuts I'll' reads as one phrase, but 'cuts' signals removing ILL from BILL, leaving B.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is old British slang for the telephone, as in get on the blower to someone.

clue.text: Having a row over a wedding gift

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a ring is given at a wedding

explanation.surface: A couple quarrelling about one of their wedding presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with cow here, a quarrel, in the surface, but the definition reads it as rhyming with toe: pulling oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaring means propelling a boat with oars, so rowing it.

clue.text: Crook from extremely eventful cockney area

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of eventful

parts.note: Bow is a district of East London; a true cockney is born within the sound of Bow Bells

explanation.surface: A villain hailing from a very lively part of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' suggests a criminal from the cockney underworld, but it means a bend. Elbow is the constable in Measure for Measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The crook of the arm is the bend at the elbow, so the joint is a crook.

clue.text: See lion trap a wild butterfly

parts.note: the letter C is named see, so the word stands for that letter
Leo, the zodiac sign, is the lion

indicators.note: a wild version of these letters is a jumbled one

explanation.surface: A lion lured into a trap, and a butterfly running free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges TRAP A into PATRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cleopatra is a yellow brimstone-type butterfly of southern Europe, Gonepteryx cleopatra.

clue.text: Gas escape from case of butane left by church

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A leak from a gas canister abandoned beside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas escape' sounds like a fuel leak but is wind from the stomach. Sir Toby Belch is in Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: A belch is a burp, wind released noisily from the stomach through the mouth.

clue.text: Sweetheart conceited European holds fast

indicators.note: the conceited piece holds the fast word inside it

parts.note: vain means conceited
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A vain European who keeps a lover at arm's length while fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like an adjective meaning firm, but it is a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a sweetheart chosen or sent a card on St Valentine's Day.
